title: Enterprise Dedicated Sizing & Fallback Orchestration for Predictable Throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a lightweight intake and prioritization rubric for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that produces a deterministic sizing recommendation (reserved throughput target, GPU-class suggestion, and scaling policy) and a fallback orchestration plan for degraded conditions. This ticket covers the PM-side questionnaire, scoring model, nominal SLA tiers, and a recommended fallback routing policy to feed into ENG and Solutions onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake questionnaire (Google Form + internal API) captures traffic profile, qps, average tokens per request, p95/p99 latency target, burst tolerance, and data residency/SLA constraints

A2: Scoring matrix outputs one of three canonical profiles (S1: baseline, S2: production, S3: mission-critical) with explicit reserved throughput units (RTU), recommended GPU family list, and burst policy
A3: Fallback orchestration defined: model variant downgrade path, cross-region failover, and degraded SLOs documented per profile
A4: Triage playbook includes escalation path, expected onboarding lead times, and cost tradeoffs for customers
A5: Stakeholder sign-off from Solutions, Runtime, and Legal recorded in comments and linked artifacts
decision: Adopt a 3-tier canonical sizing model: S1 (RTU 1-5k tokens/sec, L4-class or shared pool), S2 (RTU 5-25k tokens/sec, A100-80GB preferred), S3 (RTU >25k tokens/sec, H100-80GB + reserved pool). Default p99 SLO targets: S1 350ms, S2 200ms, S3 120ms for standard 32-token responses; allow negotiated tighter SLOs with committed spend. Fallback orchestration: try local model variant downgrade (quantized variant) -> burst to Dedicated overflow pool -> cross-region read-only routing -> notify & throttle. Autoscale policy defaults: vertical burst for <2x sustained, horizontal autoscale above sustained load with warmup window.
